Hello, I'm here from Reddit. As a long time user of reddit I had unsubscribed from most of the original default subs. The quality of each suffers from it. After you've been on reddit for a while you start to notice the same patterns of posts. Mostly low hanging fruit for reposters and karma whores with a sprinkling of good quality content. But then they added all the new subs to the default list and the quality has suffered because of it. I also didn't like the censorship going on in places such as TB thread or any thread mentioning Pao and many others.

I really like the sorting method of reddit. If I find a new subreddit I can sort by top in different time periods. It helps me get a feel of what's popular and what the sub likes looking at or discussing. Usually I'm using reddit from the "reddit is fun" app on the android so I don't get to read the sidebar usually. I use reddit a lot from my phone. I love going to the comments after reading an article and getting more information on a subject, or an alternative opinion or someone calling bullshit on a claim. This latest net neutrality ruling was a very important movement and I believe reddit helped it along. I found out about fight for the future on there which would just connect you to all the FCC representatives and your own representatives. It was cool.

So I wish voat had the same sorting option, it's own mobile app. Not some unofficial third party app which leads to dozens of apps and I think pushes away newcomers. Some may believe that having a mobile option leads to hive minding I believe good moderation can overcome that. By removing memes from most of the big subvoats we can lead to improved discussion. Maybe have a tag system for comments which are "helpful", "funny", "discussion" so that we can filter out some "joke" ones or the eventual pun threads of reddit. I just really miss the discussion and helpful comments.

I hope to be here for a while. I really like this place and I'm excited to see it grow. Hopefully it can have a helpful and courteous community that promotes discussion and higher quality content.

Let me be the first to welcome you to Voat! I do believe that a mobile app is in development, although I had no issues using it off Safari on my iPhone 4S this past weekend. Feel free to contribute any ideas you have for improvement to /v/ideasforvoat, and you should have a heads up that the amount of upvoats you have is limited to 10 until your comment score is over 20. After that, Your comment score divided by 2 will equal your daily upvoat limit. This encourages positive contributions, and in a way prevents any brigading. Nonetheless, welcome!

Thank you! I did not know about comment score contributing to the number of daily voats. That's a pretty novel idea. My only concern is that the push for comment karma might result in users going for the low hanging fruit (joke/pun threads, memes, etc,.).

I don't think voating should count to one of your own replys. You're the best judge of a reply to your own comment, right?

I really haven't seen many jokes/puns and I made pretty much the only meme I've seen on the front page. I think a lot of people here are looking to escape that part of the reddit culture, in addition to the sketchy moderation the Pao debacle.

I'm not advocating the sketchy moderation but rather the type of moderation that makes /r/nfl or /r/eatcheapandhealthy so great. I'm not even interested in the NFL but I've only heard great things about its moderators. Eatcheapandhealthy allows only self posts.

Edit: Whoaaa, I can link to subreddits with the same /r/ Cool.

I'm excited for it to grow and for the userbase to grow with it. I just hope the creators stick to their philosophy and cater to the userbase in a productive means.
